# Mid-status sheet

fixture: mid-build-status

Essay Bot uses these templates while Cursor CLI or Grok Build is doing the file work, and on any other file-work path on stages 1 to 10.
The file-work path signals a phase. Essay Bot rephrases that phase in these words.
Essay Bot does not invent a phase.
No file-work path running means no working line.
A short job has a start line and, when it is ready, the next ask. Name the Confirm card only when that stage's card is in the latest door result and the artifact is ready to lock.
It does not get a fixed five-minute line.
If the file-work path stays silent for about five minutes, say one calm still-working line, then wait for a status signal or until the step is ready.
That ping is for every file-work stage: research, draft, edits, review, and the rest. Not research only.
When a status line names the standard, use the opening already printed for this assignment.
A diary with a table uses How to score high and the printed top column.
An essay or a report with a scheme uses what the mark scheme scores.
If there is no scheme, use the brief and the assignment ask.
Never invent a band.
Do not rename a diary column to the words mark scheme.

## starts
- gathering: I have started gathering sources for {subject}.
- annotating: I have started annotating the sources for {subject}.
- notes: I have started the notes on each source for {subject}.
- drafting: I have started the first draft for {subject}.
- work: I have started work on {subject}.

## any
- start: I have started work on {subject}.
- still: I am still working on {subject}.
- ready: {subject} is ready for the next step in this chat.
- ready_confirm: {subject} is ready. Open the Confirm card to save this step.
- done_mid: I have finished the file work on {subject}.
- saved: {subject} is saved.
- exit_stopped: File work on {subject} stopped before it finished. Please wait and try this step again in this chat.
- exit_missing_tool: I could not start file work on {subject} because the writing tool is not on this computer.

## phases
- sources: I have gathered the sources for {subject}.
- annotation: I have annotated the sources for {subject}.
- notes: I have written a note on each source for {subject}.
- draft: The first draft for {subject} is ready.

## sources
- gathering: I am gathering the sources for {subject}.
- open_full: I am checking that each source for {subject} opens in full, against {basis}.
- list_notes: The source list and notes for {subject} are ready.

## deep_read
- carefully: I am reading each source for {subject} carefully against {basis}.
- helps_mark: I am noting how each source helps {basis}.
- notes_ready: The notes on the sources for {subject} are ready.

## draft
- structure: I am shaping the structure and the body for {subject}.
- nearly: The first draft for {subject} is nearly ready.
- confirm: Open the Confirm card when the draft for {subject} is the one to save.

## quality
- check: I am checking {subject} against {basis}.
- rewrite: I am rewriting the weak parts of {subject}.
- fixing: I am still fixing {subject}.
- clear: {subject} is clear against {basis}.

## ask_edit
- questions: Please answer the questions on {subject} in this chat.
- apply: I am applying those answers to {subject}.
- currency: I am checking currency and clarity for {subject}.
- heavier: This edit of {subject} is heavier than a light pass.
- confirm: Open the Confirm card to save the edit of {subject}.

## word_final
- together: I am putting the Word file together for {subject}.
- comments: I am writing the comments and findings for {subject}.
- no_submit: The final copy of {subject} does not submit.
- keep: Keep a copy of {subject}. This step does not submit.
